doc: Chapter 1, Apollo 13 (April 1970): the cuyes' scenes (issue #66; story: docs/design/story-v0.3.0.md). Every fact is from NASA's own pages, its source id in docs/sources.md. The cuyes never change history: they react; the outcome is NASA's. Lines: who, text, mood (scripts/story/cuy_actor.gd MOODS), fact + source, shot (wide, close, two, low), fx (shake, alarm, dim, calm), all (everyone's mood); a line with title (+ sub) and no who is a title card.

briefing.text: Houston here. Well, a cuy in Houston. Apollo 13 is going to the Moon.
Three astronauts, a command module, a lunar module. And us, who are not on any list.
I packed a thermometer, a notebook and snacks. Mostly snacks.
Nothing will go wrong. I checked the tanks.

problem.fact: On April 13, 1970 (Houston time), oxygen tank no. 2 exploded, about 200,000 miles from Earth.

problem.text: I checked them. I did not check them enough.
Everyone into the lunar module. It is a lifeboat now.
problem.fact: With the command module's power running out, the crew moved into the lunar module, their lifeboat.

problem.text: The air is filling with carbon dioxide. We need the command module's filters in here.
problem.fact: The command module's square CO2 canisters did not fit the lunar module's round openings.

problem.text: Mission Control sent a recipe: plastic bags, cardboard and tape.
problem.fact: Mission Control worked out an adapter from plastic bags, cardboard and tape.

home.text: Splashdown. All three astronauts are home.
Nobody landed on the Moon. Everybody came back. That counts.
Next time, can we just land somewhere?
Mars. On airbags. What could go wrong.
